title: hosted-inference-5xx-surge-correlation-and-request-fallthrough-protector
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Customer escalation: multiple large tenants reported intermittent 5xx responses and client-observed timeouts during peak hours. Investigation indicates a correlated increase in long-running inference tails leading to request retry amplification and backend KV-cache thrash. This ticket coordinates investigation, immediate mitigations, and a staged permanent fix to prevent recurrence across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private routing layers.
impact: High — several enterprise customers experienced request failures and elevated latency (99th p99 latency from ~250ms to ~4s) resulting in degraded UX and two escalations to CS/AM.
repro_steps: 1) Simulate 1:20 burst of long sequence requests against model X-8k with concurrent tenant uploads. 2) Enable heavy prefix cache invalidation (TTL=0) while running influx of small chat messages. 3) Observe edge queue lengths, backend worker busy counts, and retry storms from SDKs.
investigation: Telemetry: per-tenant trace sampling showed a spike in backend execution tails and a corresponding rise in client-side retries (exponential backoff not honored by older SDKs). Host-level metrics show KV-cache eviction spikes correlated with GC on nodes running mixed-hosted/dedicated workloads. Root-cause hypothesis: (a) long-tail inference requests congest sequence-processing worker pools, (b) aggressive client retries amplify load, (c) KV-cache eviction race causes extra cold-start overhead, producing 5xx timeouts from overloaded runtime threads.
temp_mitigation: 1) Deploy tenant-scoped soft-quarantine: throttle request admission for implicated tenants for 30m windows. 2) Apply edge-level conservative retry gate: drop non-idempotent retries when inflight request backlog > configured threshold. 3) Patch SDK guidance: force client backoff >= 800ms for older SDK versions during incident. 4) Increase kvcache claim grace period to reduce thrash (hosted runtime flag).
permanent_plan: A) Implement per-tenant inflight caps with priority admissions and low-latency fastpath for priority customers. B) Add request fingerprinting + idempotency token enforcement at edge to safely drop/merge duplicate retries. C) KV-cache eviction smoothing: background compaction and lease-based cache leasing to avoid mass invalidations. D) Runtime: separate long-sequence worker pool and adaptive preemption to prevent tail tasks from starving short requests.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Ship edge retry gate + tenant inflight cap to 5% of hosts for one weekend (console flag: incident-protector-canary). Monitor p95/p99, error-rate, and customer feedback for 48h. Phase 2: Expand to 50% with emergency rollback gates. Phase 3: Full rollout with runtime changes during scheduled maintenance (requires Dedicated choreography).
monitoring: Add new dashboards: 'Tenant Inflight by Priority', 'Edge Retry Gate Drops', 'KV Eviction Burst Rate'. Alerts: trigger when tenant error-rate > 2% and retry-gate-drops > 5% of requests over 10m. Retention: keep 1s granularity for 24h and 1m for 30d for troubleshooting.
customer_communication: Sent initial incident e-mail to affected accounts with mitigation steps and ETA for fixes. Template ID: COMM-2025-02-20-ESCL. PM to follow up with individualized timelines and optional emergency compensation. Postmortem to be published within 7 days.
